skill.name: react-best-practices
skill.description: React and Next.js performance guidance for agents that write, review, or refactor application code. It focuses on waterfalls, bundle size, server rendering, data fetching, re-render control, and JavaScript hot paths.
skill.summary: Apply React and Next.js performance rules while generating or reviewing frontend code.

content.value_statement: React and Next.js apps often suffer from slow data fetching, large bundles, and avoidable re-renders. This skill gives agents concrete rules and examples for performance-focused code generation and review.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to avoid async waterfalls with parallel fetching and Suspense boundaries.
Guides bundle reduction with direct imports, dynamic imports, and delayed third-party loading.
Covers server-side React patterns such as React.cache, LRU caching, and RSC boundary serialization.
Shows client-side data fetching patterns with SWR and shared event subscriptions.
Provides re-render and JavaScript hot path rules with incorrect and corrected examples.
Organizes rules by impact so agents can prioritize high-value changes first.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not execute code or measure application performance directly.
Some examples depend on project versions, such as Next.js features and modern React APIs.
It cannot prove that a proposed optimization improves a specific app without profiling.
It focuses on performance patterns, not complete accessibility or security review.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Use the rules to identify waterfalls, broad imports, excess serialization, and render churn before merging React changes.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Slow Page
use_cases.description: Apply the highest-impact async, bundle, and server rendering guidance to improve a slow Next.js route.

use_cases.title: Generate Performant Components
use_cases.description: Ask an agent to create React components that use stable state updates, narrow effects, and appropriate lazy loading from the start.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one React component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component with the React best practices skill. Focus on avoidable re-renders, effect dependencies, state updates, and expensive work.

prompt_templates.title: Find Data Waterfalls
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Next.js page for data fetching waterfalls. Suggest which awaits can run in parallel and where Suspense boundaries would improve initial rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Bundle Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these imports and client components for bundle size issues. Recommend direct imports, dynamic imports, delayed third-party loading, and preload points.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Performance Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this React or Next.js feature using the skill rules. Rank findings by expected impact, explain tradeoffs, and propose focused code changes with tests.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard page that awaits user, config, and metrics one after another.
output: The review identifies an async waterfall because independent requests run sequentially.
It recommends starting independent promises early and awaiting them together when values are needed.
It notes where a Suspense boundary can show surrounding layout before metrics finish loading.

output_examples.input: Ask for bundle guidance on a component that imports an icon library barrel and a heavy editor.
output: The response flags broad imports and a heavy initial component dependency.
It recommends direct package imports or Next.js optimized package imports for icons.
It suggests dynamic loading for the editor and preloading on hover or focus.

output_examples.input: Ask how to reduce re-renders in a form with changing callbacks and derived state.
output: The response recommends functional state updates for callbacks that depend on current state.
It suggests subscribing to derived boolean state instead of continuous values when possible.
It narrows effect dependencies to primitive values used by the effect.

best_practices: Apply critical rules first, especially async parallelization and bundle size reduction.
Use the examples as review guidance, then adapt changes to the project framework and version.
Verify performance-sensitive changes with profiling, tests, or bundle analysis when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every micro-optimization before addressing obvious data waterfalls or bundle bloat.
Do not add memoization or caching without checking dependency correctness and invalidation needs.
Do not copy examples blindly when project constraints, versions, or user data handling differ.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or modify files by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an AI agent or developer can apply during code generation and review.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it target?
faq.answer: It targets React and Next.js, with several rules specific to React Server Components and Next.js routing patterns.

faq.question: Can it replace performance profiling?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify likely issues, but real applications still need profiling and measurement.

faq.question: Does it cover security best practices?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. The content is performance-focused and should be paired with a separate security review.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: How should teams adopt the rules?
faq.answer: Start with critical data fetching and bundle rules, then apply render and JavaScript rules where profiling shows a problem.
